title.narrative: Conexion GUA - Resilient Ecosystems Supporting Women and Youth Livelihoods
Conexion GUA - Resilient ekosystem som stödjer kvinnors och ungas försörjning

description.narrative:
Den önskade effekten av Conexion Guatemalas ingripande är att ge människor, främst ungdomar och kvinnor från landsbygdens etniska ursprungsbefolkning, möjlighet att bygga hållbara och motståndskraftiga försörjningar i ett samhälle som respekterar deras rättigheter. De föreslagna tre effekterna i var och en av utvecklingsmodellerna är:
1) Ungdom/sysselsättning/entreprenörskap: Ungdomar på landsbygden och i stadsnära områden och kvinnor i situationer med socioekonomisk utsatthet får omfattande utbildning och förbättrar sina sysselsättnings- och entreprenörskapsmöjligheter, samtidigt som de är förändringsagenter som till fullo utövar sina rättigheter.
2) Resilient Forest Communities: Agroskogsproducenter, särskilt unga människor och kvinnor från skogssamhällen, förbättrar sin inkomst efter att ha stärkt och diversifierat sina aktiviteter och produktiva företag från hållbar skogsförvaltning och begränsning av klimatförändringar.
3) Ledarskap och kommunikationsförmåga hos unga kvinnliga och manliga ledare: Ungdomsgrupper leder och främjar processer för socialt och politiskt inflytande för att deras rättigheter ska kunna genomdrivas (inklusive rätten till ett liv fritt från våld) och synliggör möjligheterna, behoven och möjligheterna för deras territorier.
Bidraget implementeras i Alta Verapaz och Peten avdelningar där Conexion redan har etablerat lokala partners och meritlista.

The desired impact of Conexion Guatemala intervention is to empower people, mainly rural ethnic indigenous youth and women, to build sustainable and resilient livelihoods in a society which respects their rights. The proposed 3 effects in each of the development models are:
1) Youth/Employment/Entrepreneurship: Rural and peri-urban youth and women in situations of socioeconomic vulnerability are comprehensively trained and improve their employment and entrepreneurship opportunities, while being agents of change who fully exercise their rights.
2) Resilient Forest Communities: Agroforestry producers, especially young people and women from forest communities, improve their income after strengthening and diversifying their activities and productive enterprises from sustainable forest management and climate change mitigation.
3) Leadership and Communication Skills of Young Female and Male Leaders: Youth groups lead and promote processes of social and political influence for the enforceability of their rights (including the right to life free of violence) and make visible the possibilities, needs and opportunities of their territories.
The contribution is implemented in Alta Verapaz and Peten departments where Conexion has already established local partners and track record.

The main objective is to implement 12-month demonstrative pilot project that operationalizes Conexion intervention models in Alta Verapaz and Peten, empowering indigenous Mayan youth and women to build sustainable and resilient livelihoods in a society that recognizes their rights. The Swedish contribution to the project is 6 000 000 SEK. The project aims to support 6 630 rural youth and women in employment and entrepreneurship, economic empowerment and enforceability of rights.

The PASOS pilot project was implemented during a 21-month period in 8 municipalities of Alta Verapaz and 4 in Peten with a total funding of 7 520 000 SEK. The project was implemented in coordination with local partners: Asociacion de Comunidades Forestales de Peten (ACOFOP), Alianza Mesoamericana de Pueblos y Bosques, Fundacion Talita Kumi and Asociacion Cristiana de Jovenes (YMCA). Strategic alliances included Ministry of Labour, Ministry of Education, municipal Youth Offices, municipal Directions for Women, mayors, and Friends of MISKA local business owners network.
Given that the Swedish cooperation strategy identifies rural, indigenous Mayan women as the main target population, 79% of project participants were rural women in predominantly Mayan indigenous territories. Training modules included Comprehensive technical training course in gastronomy, short courses in gastronomy and, digital and business skills in modalities of permanent schools and mobile school "MISKA" which attended three remote, rural municipalities in northern Alta Verapaz department.
Through PASOS, 190 youth and women (between the age of 16-25) now have certificates as Kitchen Assistant Technicians, impacting positively in the quality of life of 950 family members, which in turn has contributed to contributing to activation of local economies. Additionally, 350 youth and women received training and capacity building through the short courses in gastronomy, promoting economic empowerment via income generation capacities. 182 youth received training in entrepreneurship, converting them from job seekers to employers in many cases by hiring other youth in their small business ventures. 223 youth and women entered the labor force in the fields of gastronomy and tourism posterior to their participation in PASOS.
The mobile MISKA school, which operated in the hard-to-reach Franja Transversal del Norte, trained 384 youth and women out of whom 21% created small businesses posterior to the training received. 1 180 indirect beneficiaries are reported from this action line. In the municipality of Fray Bartolome de las Casas the MISKA mobile school was implemented in coordination with the municipal office for planning and development.
55 women received seed money to create their own small businesses. The action included personalized technical assistance to calculate production costs, create a brand, support in marketing strategies, digital skills, and registration with tax authorities to comply with tax regulation.
154 youth were trained in digital skills, which has helped increase their economic opportunities while contributing to reduction of the digital divide.
40 public-private strategic alliances were established. This has had a catalyzing impact in expanding the project and strengthening its results. Agreements were signed with 4 municipalities in Alta Verapaz, and 36 Letters of Understanding were formalized with businesses in the food industry sector.
As for results in Peten, Conexion supported ACOFOP actions in the Community Forest Concessions through seed money for small business ventures in community tourism and agroforestry initiatives, while providing capacity building to ACOFOP technical teams on Conexion intervention methodologies. Conexion (previously ICCO Cooperation) has over twenty-year experience of cooperating with ACOFOP and these mutually respectful working relations have opened doors for PASOS to effectively support the forest communities. This experience and already established relations permitted Conexion to participate as local implementing partner to Swisscontact in the TEI Peten Mas Sostenible/Paisajes Mayas Sostenibles project.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
